steps.title: Conditional probability
steps.content: Conditional probability measures the chance of event A given that event B has happened. Restrict the sample space to outcomes where B is true.
steps.formula: P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B), when P(B) > 0
steps.example: If 3 of 5 red balls are marked, then P(marked | red) = 3/5.

steps.title: Calculate a conditional probability
steps.prompt: A bag has 4 red and 6 blue balls. Of the red balls, 2 are marked. What is P(marked | red)?
steps.explanation: Given that the ball is red, the sample space contains only 4 red balls. Two are marked, so 2/4 = 1/2.

steps.title: Independent events
steps.content: Events A and B are independent when knowing that one occurred does not change the probability of the other. For independent events, P(A∩B)=P(A)×P(B).
steps.example: Two fair coin tosses are independent. P(heads on both) = 1/2×1/2 = 1/4.

steps.title: Use the complement
steps.prompt: A fair die is rolled twice. What is the probability of getting at least one 6?
steps.explanation: Use the complement: P(no 6 on either roll) = 5/6×5/6 = 25/36. At least one 6 = 1−25/36 = 11/36.

steps.title: Use total probability carefully
steps.content: When outcomes are separated into mutually exclusive cases that cover all possibilities, add the probability of the event within each case multiplied by the probability of that case.
steps.example: If a product comes from factory A or B, calculate the probability of a defect from each factory and weight it by the factory's production share.
steps.tip: Draw a tree diagram when events happen in stages or depend on earlier outcomes.
